The managed server operates within Snowflake accounts, where underlying compute and AI usage can consume billable credits; exact costs depend on account agreement, region, edition, workload, and configured services.

B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Snowflake bills account usage under its consumption pricing model. Queries and configured services can consume warehouse credits or other billable usage. No MCP-specific per-call rate or quota price was found.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Clients discover and invoke tools using tools/list and tools/call. Each MCP server object is configured with one or more tools, chosen from Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, SQL execution, Cortex Agent, Coding Agent, and GENERIC UDF or stored-procedure tools. Names and input schemas depend on the account's specification.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool results use MCP content results. As of August 20, 2026, tools/call responses are returned as an SSE stream; clients should accept application/json and text/event-stream. The stream ends with data: [DONE].

Snowflake OAuth is the default; customers can bind an External OAuth identity provider. OAuth sessions use the connecting user's DEFAULT_ROLE by default. Administrators can configure OAUTH_SCOPES_SUPPORTED, ALLOWED_ROLES_LIST, redirect URIs, and secondary-role behavior. The supplied pre-fetch says no public metadata was fetched because the input is not a concrete URL, so endpoint-specific metadata and raw scope values are unavailable.

C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Snowflake OAuth by default, or External OAuth. OAuth 2.0; public clients can use PKCE; confidential clients use a client secret. Dynamic Client Registration is not supported. By default, the advertised scope is session:role:all. Configurable primary-role scopes include session:role-any and session:role:<role_name>; administrators can set OAUTH_SCOPES_SUPPORTED. The provided metadata result: NOT FETCHED because endpoint is per-customer/not public. Token lifetime and revocation details were not found in the reviewed MCP-specific pages.

Cortex Agent and Coding Agent tools can use continuation state via thread_id and parent_message_id when ENABLE_MCP_AGENT_RUN_THREAD_CONTINUATION is enabled (default on). Coding Agent runs receive a managed sandbox; a code_toolset_all tool is appended. This is per-tool conversation state, not a general MCP memory feature.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Agent tool result contains the agent reply and thread_id; coding-agent sandbox persists with its conversation thread.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The server supports read-oriented Search, Analyst, and optional read-only SQL tools; GENERIC and Agent tools can perform writes. Optional annotations include readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, and openWorldHint. For GENERIC and CORTEX_AGENT_RUN, defaults are false/true/false/true respectively; these are client hints, not enforced controls. 2. No universal confirmation flow is documented. 3. Access uses OAuth or PAT; permissions inherit Snowflake role grants on the server and its underlying objects. OAuth scopes control the primary role; secondary roles are separately configured. 4. Administrators define server tool composition and can use separate server objects and roles. SQL read_only defaults true; response cap and recursion limits apply. 5. Documentation says role-based access and masking policies apply; no MCP-specific PII masking logic is described. 6. Maximum 50 tools per server; generic and SQL results truncate at 250 KB; query_timeout is configurable for SQL and generic tools; recursion depth is capped at 10. 7. Input schemas are specified for GENERIC tools; no general MCP-specific correction or override behavior is documented. 8. MCP-specific audit logging and telemetry details: Unknown. 9. No feedback/rating/marketing tools identified in the documented quickstart list; configured custom tools can vary. 10. Tool descriptions and optional Coding Agent instructions are administrator-provided; client-facing annotation hints are not enforced. 11. Agent/coding-agent continuation can persist by thread ID when enabled; default is on. 12. Server uses configurable tool objects; Cortex Agent and Coding Agent may orchestrate nested tools. 13. SYSTEM_EXECUTE_SQL is an unrestricted SQL surface unless configured read_only=true; SQL is an escape hatch around agent semantic views and orchestration. Snowflake warns of that bypass.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No fixed official tool list exists for every account endpoint: administrators define the tool array in each MCP server object. The official CREATE MCP SERVER reference lists six supported tool types, not a fixed set of names. The official Getting Started guide states that its example server exposes four tools; those four quickstart names are in actions.json as the best available concrete list, not a claim about the unspecified input account's configuration. No catalogue-only tools were added. Third-party catalogues describe other Snowflake integrations or variants and do not establish the tools of this account endpoint.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Snowflake users can perform account, database, schema, warehouse, object, access-control, and administrative operations through Snowflake interfaces and SQL. The managed MCP server exposes only the tools configured in its tool array, up to 50; the reviewed guide's example exposes only four tools and does not expose general server administration. F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Snowflake recommends least privilege, OAuth, checking tool definitions, and avoiding recursive loops. It warns that tool annotations are client-facing hints and do not enforce behavior. Quote: "Tool annotations are client-facing hints, not security controls."
F_documentation.governance_promises: Snowflake describes governance through RBAC and says data masking policies can govern MCP access. The privacy policy says customer content is retained under the customer agreement. No MCP-specific telemetry opt-out, retention period, or AI-training statement was found in the reviewed pages.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The managed server is presented as a way to expose Snowflake data tools without deploying separate infrastructure, while using the same role-based access controls as the account.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: RBAC is implemented through Snowflake privileges on the MCP server and its configured objects. SQL read_only and tool annotations are configuration options; annotations are explicitly non-enforcing. Result truncation, tool-count and recursion limits are documented server-side. Privacy-policy retention terms are general service terms, not specific MCP-call controls.

observations_for_research: Tool names, descriptions, schemas, and behavior are configured by the account administrator, so the same vendor-managed endpoint class can expose materially different agent capabilities per customer.
The endpoint host and OAuth metadata are account-specific; the provided input does not identify one concrete server object or published URL.
The administrator-configurable SYSTEM_EXECUTE_SQL tool can be set read-only or configured with broader SQL permissions, changing whether the client can bypass Cortex Agent orchestration.
